{
  "thinking": "Priya's worry about the fin prongs is fair: they point back at a steep angle, so the fall may not catch. Hana and Maya have the edges going, and I want to watch the nose join and the tail end before anyone builds on them. My hands are free, but I'll wait for the strokes rather than place dominoes early.",
  "say": "Priya, good catch on the fin angle. Hana and Maya, I'm keeping an eye on the nose where your two edges meet, and I'll look at the tail end once the top edge is standing. If the prongs won't catch, a short angled bridge might fix it. I'm not touching anything until the strokes are down.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 3,
  "point": [3, 8],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Fish facing right, tail on left, START at tail tip (about 1.5,10). Stroke 1 = top edge (Hana, from the tail). Stroke 2 = bottom edge (Maya, traced from the tail tip). Strokes 4 and 5 = tail fin prongs off the top and bottom edges near the back. Stroke 3 = forked tail (Sofia traces once it's on the pad). Eye is a label, still open. Priya thinks the fin prongs may not catch (they point back at a steep angle; the fall only jumps about 40 degrees off the line). Possible fix: an angled bridge at the prong joints. I'm watching the tail-tip junction and the nose join. Nothing in my hands. Wait for strokes before building. Possible fix at the nose if the edges don't meet cleanly."
